title: Generic Structs and Impl Blocks
goal: Define data structures and methods that work across any type.

sections.text: You know generic classes from Java or C++ templates. In Rust, generic structs group fields whose types are decided when instantiated.

sections.caption: <T> introduces the generic type parameter on the struct.

sections.text: When adding methods to a generic struct, you write `impl<T> Container<T>`. The first `<T>` declares the type parameter for the block.

sections.caption: The first <T> tells Rust that T is a generic parameter, not a concrete type.

sections.text: Declaring `<T>` on `impl` allows defining methods for any `T`. You can also write `impl Container<i32>` to define methods available only for `i32`.

sections.caption: Methods in this block only exist when T is i32.

sections.text: Leaving off the first `<T>` causes compiler error `E0412` because Rust looks for a concrete type named `T`.

explanation: Define data structures and methods that work across any type.
